blocks.html: WhatsApp Flows let a business turn an ordinary chat into a guided, multi-step form customers choose options, enter details and finish a task like booking, registration or an application without ever leaving the conversation. For years the pattern was the same: a customer taps a link, gets thrown onto an external landing page or a long web form, and quietly abandons it halfway. Every redirect and every extra field is another chance to lose them. Keeping the whole exchange inside the chat window strips that friction out, and it is why so many teams are rebuilding their sign-up and booking journeys this way.

This guide walks through what these interactive forms are, the components that make them work, how a full journey runs end to end, what they cost in India, and how to build one without touching code. Everything below assumes your number is already live on the WhatsApp Business API — and Ojiva AI is an official Meta Business Solution Provider for India that sets up and manages these journeys on your behalf.

sections.heading: What In-Chat Forms Do That Landing Pages Cannot

blocks.html: An in-chat form is exactly what it sounds like: a structured, screen-like experience that opens inside the chat instead of sending the customer somewhere else. Where a plain conversation is back-and-forth text, WhatsApp forms present clean fields, dropdowns and buttons that feel closer to a lightweight app. The customer stays in a place they already trust and use every day, which is the whole reason completion holds up so well.

items.desc: The experience runs where daily conversations already happen, which lowers hesitation at the point of action.

sections.heading: How Encryption Protects the Data Customers Share

blocks.html: When a journey needs to talk to your own systems in real time — checking availability, pulling a quote — the data moving between the customer and your endpoint is encrypted, not sent in the clear. This is where WhatsApp Business encryption matters. Meta requires you to generate a key pair and upload the public key, which Meta then signs, and the request and response payloads are encrypted between the app and your server. It is a genuine security model, and worth understanding rather than glossing over.

items.title: A signed key pair:
items.desc: You generate keys and upload the public one, which Meta signs before any encrypted exchange begins.

items.title: Encrypted payloads:
items.desc: Incoming requests are decrypted on your endpoint and responses re-encrypted before they return to the customer.

items.title: Sensitive data stays protected:
items.desc: The model exists specifically so details like contact and payment information are not exposed in transit.

blocks.html: The exact contract is laid out in Meta's endpoint implementation documentation, which covers key upload, request signing and payload encryption in full.

sections.heading: What These Journeys Cost in India

blocks.html: Interactive forms do not carry a separate line-item price of their own — they ride inside WhatsApp conversations, and the conversation category is what sets the rate. In practice the cost sits alongside the template or session that delivers the form, billed in INR with 18% GST on top. Because Meta sets and periodically revises the rate card, the sensible approach is to judge cost per completed outcome rather than per message.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Interactive Chat Forms

items.q: What is a WhatsApp Flow and how does it work?
items.a: It is an interactive, multi-step form that runs inside a WhatsApp chat. A customer opens it from an entry point like an ad or a button, works through screens of fields, dropdowns and buttons, and their answers sync to your systems in real time — all without leaving the conversation.

items.q: Can you build one without any coding?
items.a: Yes. A no-code builder lets you assemble screens, add fields and buttons, connect your CRM and publish — no development team needed. Ojiva AI sets the whole thing up for you as an official Meta Business Solution Provider.

items.q: Do these journeys need DLT registration in India?
items.a: No. DLT registration under TRAI rules applies to SMS. Messages on WhatsApp are verified through Meta's own template and business review process instead, so a chat-based form does not require DLT.

items.q: Is the data customers share actually encrypted?
items.a: Yes. When a journey exchanges data with your endpoint, Meta requires an uploaded, signed public key and encrypts the request and response payloads. Sensitive details are protected in transit rather than sent in the clear.

items.q: How much do they cost in India?
items.a: There is no separate charge for the form itself — cost follows the WhatsApp conversation that carries it, billed per conversation in INR with 18% GST. Marketing conversations sit at the premium rate; utility ones are lower. Ask Ojiva AI for the current rate card before planning volumes.

items.q: How are these different from Google Forms?
items.a: A Google Form lives on an external page the customer has to open in a browser and then return from. A chat-based form runs inside the conversation itself, so there is no redirect and no waiting for a page to load, and completion tends to hold up better as a result.

items.q: Can responses connect to my CRM?
items.a: Yes. Answers can push straight into your CRM, helpdesk, scheduling tool or spreadsheet the moment they are submitted, so leads and bookings appear automatically without manual entry.

items.q: Which industries and business sizes can use them?
items.a: Almost any — e-commerce, healthcare, education, banking, insurance, travel, real estate and support teams all use them. Small businesses benefit as much as large ones, since a no-code setup needs no technical team or heavy infrastructure.
